I can only speak to the facilities I've worked in/rotated through the the state I'm licensed, but yes. Your state (country?) may be different but at my current facility we don't have CNA's specifically, we have 'techs' in the ED and 'patient care assistants' up on the floor, neither of which requires certification pre-hire. This isn't really "ice cream" in the traditional sense, but a frozen, delicious, cream-based dessert. Also kinda of a fat bomb.

1/2 bar of Lindt 90% dark chocolate (or 95% if you can find it) 4 oz. cream cheese 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream 2 tbsp erythritol 1 tbsp special dark cocoa

In a double boiler or similar contraption, melt the Lindt chocolate. In a separate bowl or KitchenAid, whip heavy cream until a nice whipped cream is formed. Combine melted chocolate, cream cheese, dark cocoa, and erythritol into mixer or bowl with whipped cream, and mix the shit out of it until you've got a nicely formed, light brown glob of deliciousness. I split it up into two servings because my wife would kill me if I ate it all, then freeze for a half hour to an hour before devouring.

Each serving:

~7.75 net carbs (11.5g gross - 3.75 dietary fiber), 450 calories, 41.75g fat, 27.75g saturated fat
